fieldsBefore.stem: Ash dieback is a serious disease of ash trees caused by the invasive pathogen Hymenoscyphus fraxineus, which originates in Asia and was brought to Europe in the early 1990s. Ash dieback was first detected in the Republic of Ireland in October 2012 on plants imported from continental Europe. The disease is now prevalent throughout most of the island of Ireland and is likely to cause the death of the majority of the ash trees over the next two decades. This will also have an effect on organisms that feed on ash (such as moths) and other animals along the food chain (such as birds, e.g. the robin). Teagasc, the Irish agriculture development authority, is aiming to establish a gene bank composed of genotypes of ash trees that are tolerant or resistant to the deadly pathogen with the future aim of producing planting stocks for forests and hedgerows in Ireland. No letters are pre-printed — the candidate writes the F — so labelKey is EMPTY rather than padded with a tautological "Skull" entry; build-deck.mjs derives figure.lettersVisible from labelKey, and any entry here would publish the crop as carrying a label it does not have, which the manifest's alt text explicitly warns against. With an empty labelKey the build emits this as a question card carrying its figure, the same shape as the other letterless figure cards in the deck. questionText and stem are verbatim from biology-2021-OL-paper1.pdf p.7. The scheme answer names a real anatomical location ("either long bone in the upper leg (thigh)"), so this is a content-bearing identification rather than a content-free "correctly positioned" criterion. Tariff is Q7's whole-question ordered split 2(6) + 3(2) + 2(1) over the seven responses in (a)–(f), so no per-part value exists: marks null against the 20-mark question total, matching the shipped Q7(a)/(e)/(f) cards. Q7(b)–(c) is NOT authored: (c) turns on "the synovial joint you have labelled X", and X exists only once the candidate writes it, so no honest label key can decode it.

selectionScan.disposition: Cover rubric, Section A: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Cover rubric, Section B: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Cover rubric, Section C: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section A rubric repeated.
Q1 lead-in: every part asked, one card per letter.
Q2(a) "in the following list": every tissue type asked, one card per tissue.
Q2(b) "1 or 2": the answer options.
Q3 lead-in: every statement asked, one card per letter.
Q3 "true or false": the answer options.
Q3 "T or F": the answer options.
Q4(e) lead-in "Answer the following": both romans asked.
Q4(e) "either of the above disorders": the scheme prints a separate cause list and treatment list for each, so each is a route card.
Q5 list of terms: the options; every description matched, one card per letter.
Q6 "Complete the following cross": every line of the cross asked, one card per line.
Section B rubric repeated.
Q7(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q8(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q9(b) "each of the following": every item asked, one card per roman.
Q9(b)(vii) "Starch agar or milk agar": one item named either way; one answer.
Section C rubric repeated.
Q10(a) lead-in: every term asked, one card per roman.
Q10(c) passage "giant deer or 'Irish Elk'": passage text.
Q10(c) passage "severe cold or over-hunting": passage text.
Q10(c)(vi) "Name either one of the two": one response, either naturalist; one row.
Q11(a) lead-in: every term asked, one card per roman.
Q11(c)(ii) "agriculture, industry or the home": description; marked on the same rows.
Q11(c)(iv) "agriculture, fisheries or forestry": description; marked on the same row.
Q12(a) lead-in: every part asked, one card per roman.
Q12(b)(ii) "Name any two bacterial shapes": one menu, claim two.
Q12(c) lead-in: every part asked.
Q13(a)(ii) "each of the following processes": both processes asked, one card each.
Q13(a)(ii) "anabolism or catabolism": the answer options.
Q13(b)(v) "aerobic respiration or anaerobic respiration": the answer options.
Q14 "any two of (a), (b), (c)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q14(a) lead-in: every part asked.
Q14(a)(iii) "Name any two of these groups": one menu, claim two.
Q14(a)(iv) "positive (+) or negative (−)": description.
Q14(a)(iv) "contains or does not contain": description.
Q14(b)(v) "each of the following": both processes asked, one card each.
Q15 "any two of (a), (b), (c)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q15(a)(ii) "a stem, a root, a bud or a leaf": the answer options for each example.
Q15(a)(iii) "from the following list": every function asked, one card each.
Q15(c)(v) "Name any two types of neuron": one menu, claim two.
Q15(c)(vi) "Clearly choose either of these disorders": the scheme prints a separate cause and treatment for each, so each is a route card.
Q15(c)(vi) "either of these disorders": the same choice; route cards.

selectionScan.disposition: Cover rubric, Section A: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Cover rubric, Section B: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Cover rubric, Section C: whole-question choice; every question is carded.
Section A rubric repeated.
Q1 lead-in: every part asked, one card per letter.
Q2 lead-in: every statement asked, one card per letter.
Q2 "true (T) or false (F)": the answer options.
Q2 "T or F": the answer options.
Q2(b) statement "in test tubes or Petri dishes": the statement's own words.
Q3(b) "asexual or sexual reproduction": the answer options.
Q4 "Choose each term": every description matched, one card per lettered part.
Q4 list of terms: the options.
Q5 lead-in: every part asked, one card per letter.
Q6 lead-in: every part asked, one card per letter.
Q6(a) "released or absorbed": the answer options.
Section B rubric repeated.
Q7(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q8(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q9(a)(i) "Give any one base pair": one answer; the scheme prints the two pairs as alternatives.
Q9(a)(ii) "changes in DNA or chromosomes": description.
Q9(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Section C rubric repeated.
Q10(a) lead-in: every term asked, one card per roman.
Q10(b)(i) "the following steps": the four steps to be ordered; one card.
Q10(c) "Copy the following": every line of the cross asked, one card per line.
Q11(a) lead-in: every term asked, one card per roman.
Q11(b)(vi) "damaged or harmed": description.
Q11(c) passage "mice or rats": passage text.
Q11(c) passage "barns or old buildings": passage text.
Q12(a)(ii) "each of the following": both items asked, one card each.
Q12(a)(ii) "mechanical or chemical digestion": the answer options.
Q12(c) passage "Irritable bowel syndrome or IBS": passage text.
Q13(b)(iii) "oxygenated or deoxygenated": the answer options.
Q14 "any two of (a), (b), (c)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q14(a)(ii)1 "a plant cell or an animal cell": the answer options.
Q14(a)(v) "selectively permeable or semi-permeable": description.
Q15 "any two of (a), (b), (c)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
Q15(a)(v) "seeds or fruits": description.

Q4(a) "each of the following pairs of kingdoms": every pair asked, one card each.

Q7(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q8(a) lead-in: every part asked.
Q8(b) lead-in: every part asked.

Q9(b)(ii)1 "pulse rate or breathing rate": either investigation; marked on the same row.
Q9(b)(ii)2 "pulse rate or breathing rate": either; marked on the same menu.

Q11(b) lead-in: every part asked.
Q11(c) "Read the following extract": every part asked.
Q11(c)(ii) "a single gene or by many genes": the answer options.
Q12(c) lead-in: every part asked.
Q13(b)(ii) "plant or animal cells": description.

Q14(b)(i) "each of the following: dermal tissue, ground tissue, vascular tissue": every tissue located; the scheme prices the labels "3(1)".
Q14(c)(iv) "any two processes": a bounded menu, claim two.
Q15 "any two of (a), (b), (c)": whole-part choice; every part is carded.
